name: Italian Neorealism
summary: Ruined streets, ordinary people and a story with no hero. Real places, non-professional actors and light that the day provides. The camera stays at human height and records the time a thing takes.

philosophy.core_thesis: A film earns its truth by going out of the studio and showing ordinary lives in the real place, at the real pace, with no star and no neat plot.
design_principles: Shoot on location in real streets, tenements and fields, with no built set and no back projection.
Cast non-professional actors for 50% or more of the roles and let them speak in their own dialect.
Light with daylight and a bounce, at a key-to-fill ratio of 2:1 to 3:1, and avoid a hard glamour key.
Frame in 1.37:1 at eye level with a 28mm to 50mm lens and keep depth in the shot, with deep focus at f/8 to f/11.
Hold a long take of 10 to 30 s on a walk or a wait, and cut at an average shot length of 8 to 12 s.
Use a slow pan or a short tracking shot of 0.5 to 1 m/s to follow a person through a street, with no crane.
Dub the sound after the shoot, and keep the score sparse: a theme of 20 to 60 s used 3 times at most.
anti_patterns: A studio back lot and a painted backdrop
A star with a glamour key light
A tidy plot with a heroic resolution
Invisible continuity with a shot and reverse shot in every scene
A swelling score under each feeling

composition.framing: A 1.37:1 frame at eye level; the street or the room fills the frame, and the person is one part of it.
composition.staging_in_depth: Deep focus with 3 planes: a figure in front, a street or courtyard in the middle and a facade or a ruin behind.
composition.subject_placement: The figure is small to medium in the frame and off centre; a face is held in a close-up only for the key moment of the scene.

principles.rule: Frame at eye level in 1.37:1 so that the place is as large as the person in the frame.
principles.value: place 60% to 80% of the frame area, person 20% to 40%

principles.rule: Stage the action in three planes in deep focus: a person, a street and a facade.
Keep the figure small against the street, so that the surroundings press on the person.
principles.value: figure 20% to 40% of the frame height in a wide shot

principles.rule: Use daylight as the key and a bounce or a window as the only fill.
Let a walk or a wait run its real time before the cut.
principles.value: 8 to 12 s average shot, 10 to 30 s for a walk

camera_and_movement.movement: A slow pan or a short follow to keep a person in the street. The camera moves because the person moves, and it stops when they stop.
camera_and_movement.support: Tripod, a light dolly or a car mount for the street
camera_and_movement.move_speed: Walking pace, 0.5 to 1.5 m/s; pan 15° to 30° per second

lens_and_format.aperture: f/5.6 to f/11 for deep focus in daylight
lens_and_format.focus: Deep focus: the person, the street and the facade are all readable.

light.quality: Hard or soft daylight as it falls, with a bounce for the faces; no added glamour light.
light.direction: Overhead or side daylight from the street; window light inside.
light.source: The sun, the sky and a reflector

colour_and_grade.treatment: Natural black and white with a full grey scale. The print is plain, with grey stone and white linen, and the grain is part of the image.
grade_recipe: Convert to black and white and set the black point at 4% and the white point at 96%.
Keep the contrast at +5% with a long, soft shoulder for the sky.
Hold midtones at 18% grey for skin and stone and keep the sky at 80% to 90%.
Add grain at 15% to 20% to match fast 35mm stock.
Do not add a tint, a vignette or a glow.
colour_and_grade.texture: Visible silver grain, amount 15% to 20%, with a little gate weave of 0.3%

editing_and_rhythm.average_shot_length: 8 to 12 s (estimate; check Cinemetrics for each title)
editing_and_rhythm.shot_length_range: 2 s for an insert to 60 s for a long walk
editing_and_rhythm.cutting_logic: Cut when the action ends, not before. Let a walk or a wait take its time, and use a close-up for the one moment that the person cannot hide.
editing_and_rhythm.transitions: Hard cut, a slow dissolve of 1 s for a time jump, and no wipe.

sound.approach: Post-synchronised sound laid over real streets, with a bed of traffic, voices and bells.
sound.dialogue: Regional speech, non-professional voices, short and plain; speech sometimes overlaps and trails off.
sound.music: A spare orchestral or piano theme of 20 to 60 s; it enters on a few cues, and a long scene has none.
sound.loudness: −23 LUFS integrated for a restoration, with dialogue peaks at −6 dBFS

titles_and_graphics.treatment: A plain opening card, a white title on a black or a street background, and a short credit roll.
titles_and_graphics.type: A plain serif or sans-serif in upper case, white on black, 3 to 5 s for the title and 1 to 2 s for each credit.

shot_primer.opening: Open on a street or a yard in daylight with people at work; the first cut comes by 8 to 12 s.

emotion.target_response: Compassion and recognition: the viewer stays with a person in need and sees the place as it is.

use_cases: period films of poverty and work
video prompts for a postwar street scene
avoid_when: The brief needs a glossy product look or a star.
The piece needs a fast cut for a feed.

modifiers.how: Keep the location and the plain light; shoot handheld, cut a jump cut into long takes and let a character look into the lens.
Keep the street and the plain light; drop the script, shoot 16mm with a handheld camera and record the real sound on location.

sources.title: André Bazin, What Is Cinema? vol. 2 (University of California Press, 1971)
Peter Bondanella, Italian Cinema: From Neorealism to the Present (Continuum, 3rd ed., 2001)
